# Cross-Language Protocol Fixtures

These fixtures are protocol fixtures, not Python test internals.

Future Rust, TypeScript, C++, or other independent verifiers should consume this index and reproduce the expected digests, statuses, key ids, registry identity statuses, and binding fields without importing the Python simulator or conformance runner.

The included keys, backend registry, registry authority, capability declarations, conformance level catalog, DMF capability/payload fixtures, `.klein`/`.kleinc` artifact fixtures, Runbook/Execution Trace fixtures, ECRP policy/evidence fixtures, Observation v1 fixtures, HIL Readiness v1 fixtures, Recorded Device Run v1 fixtures, Generic DMF Backend Adapter v1 fixtures, OpenDrop/EWOD Adapter Skeleton v1 fixtures, OpenDrop Transport Planning v1 fixtures, Trusted Timestamp Profile v1 stub fixtures, and Attestation Profile v1 stub fixtures are public test fixtures only. Trust means authorized by the fixture Trust Policy v1 document only. Signed registry provenance and signed capability declarations are local claims, not global PKI. OpenDrop transport fixtures are dry-run command-stream planning artifacts only; they do not copy or vendor OpenDrop code, require an OpenDrop install, open serial ports, perform device IO, or claim OpenDrop hardware support. Timestamp profile/token fixtures are mock/local current-alpha shapes only; they are not TSA responses, RFC 3161 proofs, external authority evidence, or trusted timestamp proof. Attestation profile/statement fixtures are none/mock current-alpha shapes only; they are not TPM, TEE, SGX, SEV, PCR, enclave, secure-element, hardware-root, hardware identity, or hardware attestation proof. Conformance levels, DMF profile fixtures, artifact validation fixtures, trace/runbook comparison fixtures, ECRP contract/recovery fixtures, observation fixtures, HIL contract/status fixtures, recorded-run fixtures, raw-log fixtures, adapter config/status/intent fixtures, transport planning fixtures, timestamp stub fixtures, and attestation stub fixtures make claims legible and enforceable; they do not imply certified hardware capability, OpenDrop hardware support, physical truth, HIL execution, trusted timestamp, substrate attestation, hardware observation, sensor attestation, hardware recovery, physical recovery proof, or hardware attestation.
